we propose a novel approach for the estimation of the signal-to-interference ratio (SIR) in the DFT-domain for non-stationarity mixtures.

the following problems: - How to obtain a robust estimate of the SIR for non-station- ary wideband signals?

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed robust SIR estimation algorithm is a very promising approach to estimate frequency-dependent SIRs and spatial coherence functions for non-station-ary wideband signals in a robust manner.
the presented methods can be used for robust estimation of the SIR and the spatial coherence in the DFT-domain in the presence of non-stationary noise.
the proposed approach can be considered as an important contribution in the area of robust SIR estimation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an efficient method for the robust estimation of the SIR in non-stationary environments.
it can be used for a robust and efficient SIR estimation in a wide range of applications.
we propose a novel robust estimator of the SIR and spatial coherence function in the DFT-domain for non-stationarity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the robustness of the proposed estimator is significantly higher than that of other methods.
the robust estimation of the DFT-domain SIR can be performed by using the spatial coherence function as a robust estimator of the SIR in the frequency domain.
the robustness against outliers is improved by the proposed method, compared to the conventional method based on the spatial averaging of SIRs.
